mainTopic: יפת and the nations of בראשית פרק י, whether רומי or פרס will fall first, and the מזוזה in לשכת פרהדרין
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point. Even though פרס, a descendant of יפת, helped build the second בית המקדש, the שכינה rests only in the 'tents of שם', meaning the first בית המקדש. The גמרא proves that פרס comes from יפת: רב יוסף teaches that תירס, one of יפת's sons, is פרס. It then explains many other names from בראשית פרק י, and it also explains the names of the three giants the spies saw in חברון. Next comes a debate about the future. רבי teaches that רומי will fall to פרס, 'the youngest of the flock'. רבה בר עולא challenges this, and a sage in ארץ ישראל defends it by reading 'youngest' as תירס, the youngest brother. A קל וחומר also supports רבי, while רב holds the opposite: פרס will fall to רומי, and a ברייתא backs him. Finally, the גמרא returns to לשכת פרהדרין and asks why only that chamber had a מזוזה. רבא explains that for רבי יהודה, a home not used all year is not a בית, and אביי challenges this from a פסוק and from the law of a סוכה. רבא's reply to the סוכה challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The שכינה rests only in the tents of שם
steps.stepSummary: Even though יפת (Persia) was 'enlarged' by helping build the second בית המקדש, the שכינה rests only in the בית המקדש built by the descendants of שם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though 'God will enlarge יפת,' the שכינה rests only in the tents of שם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier point. The second בית המקדש, which the Persians helped build, did not have the שכינה the way the first one did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two halves. 'יפת אלהים ליפת' means יפת is given honor, since פרס helped build the second בית המקדש. 'וישכן באהלי שם' then limits that honor: the שכינה actually dwells only in a בית המקדש of שם, meaning the first בית המקדש. This explains why the second בית המקדש was missing the full presence of the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: The tents of שם, read here as the first בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source the גמרא uses to explain why the second בית המקדש lacked the שכינה, even though it was a real בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּ״יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת״ —
phrases.english: Even though "God will enlarge Japheth"
phrases.notes: Refers to the Persians (from יפת) helping to build the second בית המקדש.

phrases.english: the Divine Presence does not rest
except in the tents of Shem.
phrases.notes: The first בית המקדש, built by שלמה, a descendant of שם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּיַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (on the previous daf) about why the second בית המקדש lacked the שכינה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The Persian role in building the second בית המקדש gave honor to יפת, but the שכינה dwells only in the בית המקדש of שם.

steps.title: How do we know the Persians come from יפת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the Persians are descendants of יפת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Persians, from where do we know that they come from יפת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step. Step 1 assumed the Persians come from יפת, so now it wants a source for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading in step 1 only works if פרס really descends from יפת. The גמרא does not just assume this; it asks for proof. The answer will come from the list of nations in בראשית פרק י.

phrases.english: And the Persians, from where do we know
that they come from Japheth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the assumption made in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the Persians descend from יפת.

steps.title: The פסוק listing the sons of יפת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בראשית י:ב, which lists the seven sons of יפת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'The sons of יפת: גומר and מגוג and מדי and יון and תובל and משך and תירס.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק that lists the sons of יפת. It will next explain which nation each name refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on finding פרס somewhere in this list. None of the names says 'Persia' outright, so the גמרא has to identify each name with a known nation. This step only quotes the source; the identifications come next.

phrases.english: As it is written: "The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog
and Madai and Javan and Tuval
and Meshech and Tiras."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by bringing the relevant פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the Persians descend from יפת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית י:ב, the list of יפת's sons.

steps.title: Identifying six of יפת's sons with known nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא matches גומר, מגוג, מדי, יון, תובל and משך with nations known in its own day.
steps.simpleTranslation: גומר is Germamya; מגוג is Kandiya; מדי is Macedonia; יון means what it sounds like (Greece); תובל is Beit Unaiki; משך is Musya.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the list one name at a time and says which nation of its own time each biblical name means. This leads up to the key name, תירס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Biblical nation names were no longer in use in the גמרא's time, so each one is 'translated' into a contemporary name. יון is the only name that needs no translation; it simply means Greece. Note that מדי is identified here with Macedonia, not with Media.

keyTerms.meaning: As it sounds; its plain meaning

steps.confusionAlert: מדי here is identified as Macedonia, not as the Persian-allied Media you may know from מגילת אסתר. So פרס is not being found through מדי.

phrases.english: Gomer, that is Germamya;
Magog, that is Kandiya;
Madai, that is Macedonia;
Javan, in accordance with its plain meaning (Greece);
Tuval, that is Beit Unaiki;
Meshech, that is Musya;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the names in the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six of יפת's sons are identified with known nations; none of them is פרס.

steps.title: A dispute over the identity of תירס
steps.stepSummary: רבי סימאי (some say רבי סימון) and the רבנן disagree. One says תירס is Beit Teraiki, and the other says it is פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: About תירס, רבי סימאי and the רבנן disagree, and some say it is רבי סימון and the רבנן: one said it is Beit Teraiki, and one said it is פרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last name, תירס, and reports a disagreement about it. Only one side identifies it as פרס, which is the opinion the proof needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here, פרס has not appeared in the list, so everything depends on תירס. According to one opinion תירס is פרס, which proves the Persians come from יפת. According to the other opinion it is Beit Teraiki (Thrace). The גמרא also records uncertainty about who the disputant was: רבי סימאי or רבי סימון.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (an alternate version of who said it)

phrases.english: Tiras, they disagree about it:
Rabbi Simai and the Rabbis,
and some say it is Rabbi Simon and the Rabbis.
One said: That is Beit Teraiki,
and one said: That is Persia.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּירָס, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי סִימַאי וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the identifications from step 4 with the final, disputed name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One opinion identifies תירס as פרס, which would place the Persians among the sons of יפת.

steps.title: רב יוסף teaches that תירס is פרס
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא that clearly identifies תירס as פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: תירס is פרס.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a teaching that takes the side identifying תירס as פרס. This completes the answer to the question in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 left the identity of תירס in dispute. רב יוסף's teaching supports the view that it is פרס. That confirms the Persians descend from יפת, so the reading in step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (introduces a teaching from the תנאים)
An אמורא who often cites ברייתות and Targum-style explanations

steps.whatToRemember: The Persians come from יפת through תירס. So even though they helped build the second בית המקדש, the שכינה rests only in the 'tents of שם'.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: תִּירָס — זוֹ פָּרַס.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught: Tiras, that is Persia.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: תִּירָס — זוֹ פָּרַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports one side of the dispute in step 5 and resolves the question of step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תירס is פרס, so the Persians are descendants of יפת.

steps.title: רב יוסף identifies סבתה, רעמה and סבתכא
steps.stepSummary: Continuing through the chapter, רב יוסף identifies these names as inner and outer Sakistan, two regions 100 parsas apart whose land has a circumference of 1,000 parsas.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'סבתה and רעמה and סבתכא': רב יוסף taught: inner Sakistan and outer Sakistan. Between one and the other is one hundred parasangs, and its circumference is one thousand parasangs.
steps.whatsHappening: The question has already been answered. The גמרא now keeps explaining other names from the same chapter in בראשית, and here it identifies three names from the next list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is no longer part of the proof about פרס. It is a further explanation of the names in בראשית פרק י. רב יוסף identifies the names with two regions of Sakistan and gives their size: 100 parsas apart, with a total circumference of 1,000 parsas.

keyTerms.meaning: Sakistan, a region in the east

steps.confusionAlert: סבתה, רעמה and סבתכא are sons of כוש (from חם), not of יפת. The גמרא is just continuing through the chapter, not adding to the proof about פרס.

phrases.english: "Sabtah and Raamah and Sabteca":
Rav Yosef taught:
inner Sakistan and outer Sakistan;
between one and the other is one hundred parasangs,
and its circumference is one thousand parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְתָּה וְרַעְמָה וְסַבְתְּכָא, תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the proof to further explanations of names in the same chapter of בראשית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סבתה, רעמה and סבתכא refer to inner and outer Sakistan.

steps.title: Identifying the cities of נמרוד's kingdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the cities at the start of נמרוד's kingdom: בבל is Babylonia, ארך is Orikhut, אכד is Bashkar, and כלנה is Nufar Ninfi.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the beginning of his kingdom was בבל and ארך and אכד and כלנה': בבל means what it sounds like; ארך is Orikhut; אכד is Bashkar; כלנה is Nufar Ninfi.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps working through בראשית פרק י. It now identifies the cities where נמרוד's kingdom began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is the same as before: each biblical name is matched with a place known in the גמרא's time. בבל needs no translation, while the other three cities are given their later names.

keyTerms.meaning: As it sounds (feminine form, referring to the city)
Orikhut, the later name of ארך
Nufar Ninfi, the later name of כלנה

phrases.english: "And the beginning of his kingdom was
Babel and Erech and Accad and Calneh":
Babel, in accordance with its plain meaning;
Erech, that is Orikhut;
and Accad, that is Bashkar;
Calneh, that is Nufar Ninfi.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתְּהִי רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ בָּבֶל וְאֶרֶךְ וְאַכַּד וְכַלְנֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of name identifications from בראשית פרק י.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cities of נמרוד's kingdom are identified with places known in the גמרא's time.

steps.title: אשור is סילק
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that the land of אשור mentioned in the פסוק is the place known as סילק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Out of that land went forth אשור.' רב יוסף taught: אשור, that is סילק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through the chapter of nations in בראשית. It now matches אשור with a place people knew in its own day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of identification as the earlier steps. רב יוסף simply connects the ancient name אשור to סילק, a region of his own time. Nothing is being challenged here.

keyTerms.meaning: Assyria / the person and land named אשור
Silek, a region known in the time of the גמרא

phrases.english: 'Out of that land went forth Asshur,'
Rav Yosef taught:
Asshur, that is Silek.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: אַשּׁוּר — זֶה סִילַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of place identifications from the chapter of nations.

steps.title: Identifying נינוה, רחובות עיר and כלח
steps.stepSummary: נינוה keeps its plain meaning. רחובות עיר is פרת דמישן, and כלח is פרת דבורסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he built נינוה and רחובות עיר and כלח.' נינוה means what it says. רחובות עיר is פרת דמישן. כלח is פרת דבורסיף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the three cities that אשור built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נינוה needs no explanation because it was still known by that name. The other two cities get new names: two towns called 'פרת', one in מישן and one in בורסיף.

keyTerms.meaning: As it sounds; its plain meaning
Rechovot Ir, a city אשור built

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיִּבֶן אֶת נִינְוֵה וְאֶת רְחוֹבוֹת עִיר וְאֶת כָּלַח״,
phrases.english: 'And he built Nineveh and Rechovot Ir and Calach,'
Nineveh means what it says;
Rechovot Ir, that is Perat of Meishan;
Calach, that is Perat of Bursif.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק and lists the cities אשור built.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נינוה keeps its plain name. רחובות עיר is פרת דמישן, and כלח is פרת דבורסיף.

steps.title: רסן is אקטיספון
steps.stepSummary: רסן, the city between נינוה and כלח, is identified as אקטיספון.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And רסן, between נינוה and כלח, it is the great city.' רסן, that is אקטיספון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק and identifies the city רסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רסן is matched with אקטיספון, a well-known city in the time of the גמרא. The פסוק's closing words, 'it is the great city', are taken up in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Resen, a city between נינוה and כלח

phrases.english: 'And Resen, between Nineveh and Calach,'
it is the great city,'
Resen, that is Aktisfon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues into the next פסוק and identifies one more city.

steps.title: Which city is called the great city?
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'it is the great city' is unclear. It could describe נינוה or it could describe רסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It is the great city.' I do not know whether נינוה is the great city or whether רסן is the great city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the words 'it is the great city' could refer to either city. This sets up the next step, which will settle the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cities are named right before 'it is the great city': רסן is mentioned last, and נינוה is mentioned first. Because of how the words are ordered, the reader cannot tell which one the פסוק means.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know (a standard way of raising a doubt about a פסוק's meaning)

phrases.english: 'It is the great city':

phrases.aramaic: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם נִינְוֵה הָעִיר הַגְּדוֹלָה,
phrases.english: I do not know whether Nineveh is the great city,
or whether Resen is the great city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם נִינְוֵה הָעִיר הַגְּדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a doubt about the end of the פסוק quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which city does 'the great city' describe: נינוה or רסן?

steps.title: ספר יונה shows נינוה is the great city
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יונה calls נינוה 'a great city', so 'the great city' in בראשית must mean נינוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says, 'And נינוה was a great city to God, a three-day walk,' you must say that נינוה is the great city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a different פסוק that directly calls נינוה great.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since יונה clearly calls נינוה 'a great city', we use that פסוק to explain the unclear one in בראשית. Here one פסוק is used to clear up another.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says (introduces a clarifying פסוק)
You must say; it must be

steps.whatToRemember: The unclear 'great city' in בראשית is נינוה, as the book of יונה shows.

phrases.english: When it says:
'And Nineveh was a great city to God,'
a three-day walk across,'
you must say:
Nineveh is the great city.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״וְנִינְוֵה הָיְתָה עִיר גְּדוֹלָה לֵאלֹהִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt raised in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in יונה calls נינוה great, so נינוה is 'the great city'.

steps.title: What the names of the three giants mean
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the names אחימן, ששי and תלמי by how great or how huge each giant was.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And there were אחימן, ששי and תלמי, the children of the ענק.' It was taught: אחימן was the most skillful of the brothers. ששי made the ground like pits. תלמי made the ground into furrows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new set of names, the giants the spies saw in חברון, and explains the meaning behind each name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is read as a description. אחימן comes from 'אח' (brother) and 'מיומן' (skilled). ששי comes from 'שחיתות' (pits), because his steps left holes in the ground. תלמי comes from 'תלמים' (furrows), because his steps left grooves like a plow does.
steps.confusionAlert: These are not three nations. They are three individual giants that the spies saw in חברון.

phrases.english: 'And there were Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the children of the Anak,'
It was taught:
Ahiman: the most skilled of the brothers;
Sheshai: he makes the ground like pits;

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמַי — שֶׁמֵּשִׂים אֶת הָאָרֶץ תְּלָמִים תְּלָמִים.
phrases.english: Talmai: he makes the ground into rows of furrows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from place names to the names of people in a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The giants' names describe their skill and their enormous size.

steps.title: Another explanation: the cities each giant built
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: each giant built a city whose name sounds like his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: אחימן built ענת, ששי built אלוש, and תלמי built תלבוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a different way of understanding the three names. Here they are linked to cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 read the names as descriptions of the giants. This step instead ties each giant to a city he built. It is an alternative explanation and does not argue against the first one.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
Ahiman built Anat;
Sheshai built Alush;
Talmai built Talbush.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same three names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each giant built a city named after him.

steps.title: What 'ילידי הענק' means
steps.stepSummary: 'ילידי הענק' means they were so tall that the sun seemed to hang around their necks like a necklace.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The children of the ענק': because of their height, they wear the sun like a necklace.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining the last words of the פסוק, 'ילידי הענק'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ענק' is read as 'necklace' (as in מעניקין). The giants were so tall that the sun seemed to rest around their necks.
steps.whatToRemember: The three giants' names and the title 'ענק' all show how huge and powerful they were.

phrases.english: 'The children of the Anak':
because of their height, they wear the sun like a necklace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last phrase of the פסוק quoted in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ענק means they wore the sun like a necklace because they were so tall.

steps.title: Rome will fall into the hands of Persia
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי, in the name of רבי, says רומי will fall to פרס, based on a פסוק about 'the youngest of the flock'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said in the name of רבי: רומי is destined to fall into the hands of פרס, as it says: 'Therefore hear the plan of God that He planned for אדום, and His thoughts that He thought for the people of תימן: surely the youngest of the flock will drag them away, surely He will make their home desolate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching about the future: רומי (called אדום) will be defeated by פרס. Since step 6 identified תירס as פרס, the topic of פרס leads naturally to this teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'the youngest of the flock' will drag אדום away. רבי reads אדום as רומי and 'the youngest of the flock' as פרס. The next steps will ask how we know the flock means פרס.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said that Rabbi said:
Rome is destined to fall into the hands of Persia,
as it is said:
'Therefore hear the plan of the Lord'
that He planned for Edom,
and His thoughts that He thought for the people of Teiman:
surely the youngest of the flock will drag them away,
surely He will make their home desolate because of them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier identification of תירס as פרס by bringing a teaching about פרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רומי will fall to פרס, who is 'the youngest of the flock'.

steps.title: How do we know the flock means Persia?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא asks what shows that 'the youngest of the flock' refers to פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא objected: From where do we see that this 'youngest of the flock' is פרס?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא opens his challenge by asking for the source behind רבי's reading. This sets up the answer and the push-back that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיה never says the name פרס. So רבה בר עולא wants to know what connects 'the flock' to פרס. The word מתקיף tells us this question is the start of an objection.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows / from where is it understood?

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla objected to this:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי ״צְעִירֵי הַצֹּאן״ פָּרַס הוּא —
phrases.english: From where do we see that this 'youngest of the flock' is Persia?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading of the פסוק in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that 'the youngest of the flock' means פרס?

steps.title: Persia is called a ram in Daniel
steps.stepSummary: In דניאל, the ram stands for the kings of מדי and פרס, and a ram belongs to the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'The ram that you saw with the two horns is the kings of Media and Persia.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא himself supplies the likely source for רבי's reading: דניאל shows פרס as a ram, which is an animal of the flock. He brings it only so he can knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a ram belongs to a flock, the 'flock' in ירמיה can be linked to פרס. This answer still leaves room for a challenge, which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'The ram that you saw,'
with the two horns, is the kings of Media and Persia.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרס is shown as a ram in דניאל, so פרס is part of 'the flock'.

steps.title: Maybe the flock means Greece
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא pushes back: יון is shown as a goat in the same chapter, so the flock could just as easily mean יון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means Greece, as it is written: 'And the hairy goat is the king of Greece'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא challenges the proof. The same chapter of דניאל shows יון as a goat, which is also an animal of the flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'the flock' only means a flock animal, then both the ram (פרס) and the goat (יון) fit. So the proof does not show that פרס is the one meant, rather than יון.
steps.whatToRemember: The ram proof alone cannot decide between פרס (a ram) and יון (a goat). Step 22 answers this by reading 'youngest' as the youngest brother, תירס, which is פרס.

phrases.english: But say it is Greece,
as it is written: 'And the hairy goat is the king of Greece'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא יָוָן, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהַצָּפִיר הַשָּׂעִיר מֶלֶךְ יָוָן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from the ram in step 19 that 'the youngest of the flock' means פרס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יון is also shown as a flock animal (a goat) in the same chapter, so the proof does not single out פרס.

steps.title: A sage rejects רבה בר עולא's challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא בר סורמקי brings רבה בר עולא's challenge to ארץ ישראל. A sage there sharply rejects it as coming from someone who does not understand the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב חביבא בר סורמקי went up to ארץ ישראל, he repeated this challenge before one of the sages. The sage said to him: Someone who does not know how to explain פסוקים raises an objection against רבי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge from Step 20 travels to ארץ ישראל, and a sage there pushes it away. He is setting up his own explanation of the פסוק, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sage does not deny that יון appears as a goat. He says the challenger misread what 'youngest of the flock' points to. The real explanation follows in Step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up (from בבל to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סְלֵיק רַב חֲבִיבָא בַּר סוֹרְמַקִי,
phrases.english: When Rav Chaviva bar Surmaki went up (to Eretz Yisrael),
he said it before a certain one of the Sages,
phrases.notes: 'It' means רבה בר עולא's challenge from Step 20.

phrases.english: He (the Sage) said to him:
Someone who does not know how to explain verses
raises an objection against Rabbi?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מאן דלא ידע פרושי קראי מותיב תיובתא לרבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קשיא of Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole of רבה בר עולא's objection
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenger misread what 'the youngest of the flock' refers to.

steps.title: Youngest of the flock means the youngest brother, which is פרס
steps.stepSummary: 'The youngest of the flock' means the youngest of the brothers. רב יוסף taught that תירס, the youngest son of יפת, is פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'the youngest of the flock' mean? The youngest of his brothers. As רב יוסף taught: תירס is פרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The sage now explains the פסוק correctly, and this protects רבי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof no longer depends on animal symbols in דניאל, where both פרס and יון appear. It depends on family order: תירס is listed last among the sons of יפת, so he is 'the youngest'. Since תירס is פרס, the פסוק can only mean פרס, and the challenge about יון falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiras, the last-listed son of יפת

steps.whatToRemember: 'Youngest of the flock' equals the youngest brother, תירס, which is פרס. So רומי falls to פרס, as רבי taught.

phrases.english: What is 'the youngest of the flock'?
The youngest of his brothers.
As Rav Yosef taught:
Tiras — that is Persia.
phrases.notes: See בראשית י:ב, where תירס is the last son of יפת listed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading behind the rejection in Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Flock' refers to the animal symbols in דניאל, so it could mean יון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Youngest' refers to the youngest brother, תירס, which is פרס alone.

steps.title: A קל וחומר that רומי will fall to פרס
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי argues that if the Chaldeans, who destroyed the First Temple, fell to פרס, then surely the Romans, who destroyed the Second Temple that פרס built, will fall to פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי: רומי will one day fall into the hands of פרס, by a קל וחומר. The First Temple was built by the descendants of שם and destroyed by the כשדים, and the כשדים fell to the Persians. The Second Temple was built by the Persians and destroyed by the Romans. Isn't it only right that the Romans fall to the Persians?
steps.whatsHappening: A second source supports the same idea as רבי, that רומי falls to פרס. This time the proof is a logical argument rather than a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כשדים destroyed a Temple that other people built, yet they still fell to פרס. The Romans destroyed a Temple that פרס itself built. So פרס has even more claim to defeat them.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lesser case to a greater one

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Elai:
Rome is destined to fall into the hands of Persia,
by an a fortiori argument:
Just as the First Temple,
which the descendants of Shem built
and the Chaldeans destroyed —
the Chaldeans fell into the hands of the Persians.
The Second Temple, which the Persians built
phrases.notes: כורש allowed and supported the rebuilding.

phrases.english: and the Romans destroyed —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיִּפְּלוּ רוֹמִיִּים בְּיַד פָּרְסִיִּים?
phrases.english: is it not right that the Romans fall into the hands of the Persians?

steps.triggerLanguage: עתידה רומי שתפול ביד פרס קל וחומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a logical proof for the same position as רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רומי will fall to פרס, because the builders of the Temple will defeat its destroyers.

steps.title: רב: פרס will fall to רומי
steps.stepSummary: רב holds the opposite view: פרס will fall into the hands of רומי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: פרס will one day fall into the hands of רומי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a prediction that directly opposes the previous step. This sets up the next back-and-forth with his students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, every source said רומי falls to פרס. רב reverses the direction, which immediately seems to clash with the 'builders versus destroyers' logic of Step 23.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: עֲתִידָה פָּרַס שֶׁתִּפּוֹל בְּיַד רוֹמִי.
phrases.english: Rav said: Persia is destined to fall into the hands of Rome.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב עתידה פרס שתפול ביד רומי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing opinion to Step 23.

steps.title: Students ask: should the builders fall to the destroyers?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי object that רב's view means the builders of the Temple would fall to its destroyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: The builders into the hands of the destroyers?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב's students challenge his view on grounds of fairness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרס built the Second Temple and רומי destroyed it. It seems unjust for the builders to be defeated by the destroyers, and this is the same reasoning as the קל וחומר in Step 23.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
The builders into the hands of the destroyers?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that פרס falls to רומי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Justice says the builders of the Temple should not be defeated by its destroyers.

steps.title: רב answers: it is the King's decree
steps.stepSummary: רב agrees that it looks unjust, but says that is how the King, הקב"ה, decreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Yes, it is the King's decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב defends his view by saying this outcome is a divine decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב accepts the students' point that it seems unfair. He answers that the outcome does not follow our sense of justice. It is simply what הקב"ה has decreed.

phrases.english: He said to them: Yes,
it is the King's decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise but appeals to a divine decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Justice requires that the builders win.
steps.terutzMaskana: The outcome is a heavenly decree, even if it seems unfair.

steps.title: Another version: the Persians also destroy synagogues
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רב's answer: the Persians are destroyers too, because they tear down synagogues.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he answered: They too destroy synagogues.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב's answer, one that rejects the students' starting assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version does not appeal to a decree. It denies that פרס deserves to be called 'builders', since the Persians also destroy synagogues. So it is fair for them to fall.

phrases.english: Some say he said to them:
They too
are destroying synagogues.

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דאמרי אינהו נמי הא קא סתרי בי כנישתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to Step 25, in place of Step 26.
steps.terutzMaskana: פרס are also destroyers, so their downfall is deserved.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב with both reasons
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says that פרס will fall to רומי, and it gives both of רב's reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: פרס will one day fall into the hands of רומי. First, because they destroy synagogues. And also, it is the King's decree that builders fall into the hands of destroyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms רב's prediction. It also includes both explanations from Steps 26 and 27, so the two versions are not really in conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: רב, supported by a ברייתא, holds that פרס falls to רומי. The reasons are that the Persians destroy synagogues, and that it is a divine decree.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
Persia is destined to fall into the hands of Rome,
first, because they destroy synagogues,
and furthermore, it is the King's decree
that builders fall into the hands of destroyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's view and both of his answers.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that פרס falls to רומי

steps.title: רומי will rule the whole world for nine months before משיח
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that משיח בן דוד will not come until רומי rules the whole world for nine months. This shows רומי will conquer פרס too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: בן דוד will not come until the wicked kingdom of רומי spreads over the entire world for nine months. As it says: 'Therefore He will give them up until the time that she who gives birth has given birth; then the rest of his brothers will return with the children of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רב to back up the idea that רומי will dominate everyone, including פרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רומי will one day rule the whole world, it must conquer פרס as well. The 'nine months' comes from the פסוק's picture of a woman giving birth, since a pregnancy lasts nine months.
steps.confusionAlert: The nine-month rule over the whole world is not a separate topic. It is brought to show that רומי will rule over פרס too, which supports רב.
steps.whatToRemember: Before משיח comes, רומי will rule the entire world for nine months, the length of a pregnancy (מיכה ה:ב).

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The son of David will not come
until the wicked kingdom of Rome spreads
over the entire world for nine months,
as it is stated:
'Therefore He will give them up until the time that she who bears has borne;

phrases.aramaic: וְיֶתֶר אֶחָיו יְשׁוּבוּן עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: then the rest of his brothers will return with the children of Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דאמר רב יהודה אמר רב אין בן דוד בא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives further support for רומי's total dominance, including over פרס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's teaching based on מיכה ה:ב

steps.title: Only לשכת פרהדרין had a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that no chamber in the מקדש had a מזוזה except לשכת פרהדרין, because the כהן גדול lived there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: None of the chambers in the מקדש had a מזוזה, except לשכת פרהדרין, because it had a living space for the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story about פרס and רומי and goes back to לשכת פרהדרין. It brings a ברייתא about which chambers in the מקדש needed a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a place where someone actually lives needs a מזוזה. The other chambers were used for work or storage, so they were exempt. לשכת פרהדרין was different because the כהן גדול lived there, so it got a מזוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
A chamber or room in the מקדש (plural: chambers)
A parchment scroll attached to the doorpost of a home
The chamber where the כהן גדול stayed before יום הכפור
A living space, a place where someone resides

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the sugya: what makes a place count as a 'house' that needs a מזוזה?

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All the chambers that were in the Temple
did not have a mezuzah,
except for the Chamber of Parhedrin,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה בָּהּ בֵּית דִּירָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: in which there was a residence for the High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל הַלְּשָׁכוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The aggadic discussion of פרס and רומי is over. The גמרא returns to the main topic, לשכת פרהדרין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only לשכת פרהדרין had a מזוזה, because it was a residence for the כהן גדול.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the מזוזה there was only a rabbinic גזירה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה points out that other chambers also had living spaces but no מזוזה. So, he says, the מזוזה in לשכת פרהדרין was only a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: But weren't there several chambers in the מקדש that had living spaces, and they had no מזוזה? Rather, the מזוזה in לשכת פרהדרין was a rabbinic decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה rejects the reason the first opinion gave. He offers a different explanation for why לשכת פרהדרין had a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is: if 'someone lives there' were enough to require a מזוזה, the other living chambers would have needed one too. Since they had none, living there alone does not create an obligation from the Torah. The מזוזה in לשכת פרהדרין was added by the Rabbis.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it so that...' This opens a rhetorical challenge.
'Rather.' This introduces the speaker's own explanation.
A rabbinic decree, not a Torah obligation

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה agrees that לשכת פרהדרין had a מזוזה. He disagrees only about WHY it was there: a rabbinic גזירה, not a Torah obligation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
But weren't there several chambers in the Temple
that had a place of residence,
and yet they did not have a mezuzah?
Rather, in the Chamber of Parhedrin it was a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא כַּמָּה לְשָׁכוֹת הָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a dissent within the same ברייתא. It argues against the reasoning of the first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The chambers of the מקדש were not obligated in מזוזה from the Torah. The מזוזה in לשכת פרהדרין was a rabbinic גזירה.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה exempt the chambers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reasoning is behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step. Why does רבי יהודה think a living space in the מקדש is not truly obligated in מזוזה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: People really did live in these chambers. So we need to know which principle makes them exempt. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This asks for the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's statement in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that explains why רבי יהודה exempts the living chambers of the מקדש from מזוזה.

steps.title: A house not used all year is not a house
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that, for רבי יהודה, a home that is not built for both summer and winter does not count as a בית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יהודה holds that any house that is not made for both the summer days and the rainy days is not a house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. רבי יהודה requires a home to be lived in all year round before it counts as a 'house' for מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chambers in the מקדש were used only at certain times. For example, the כהן גדול used לשכת פרהדרין for just seven days before יום הכפור. They were not year-round homes, so they are not a בית and need no מזוזה from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The summer days, the hot season

steps.whyThisMatters: This year-round rule is the principle that אביי attacks in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
Any house that is not made
for the summer days and for the rainy days —
is not a house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יהודה, only a dwelling used all year round is a בית that needs a מזוזה.

steps.title: A verse calls a winter house a house
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא with a פסוק that calls a seasonal dwelling a 'winter house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: But it is written, 'I will strike the winter house together with the summer house'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's rule using a פסוק in עמוס. The פסוק uses the word 'house' for a home that is used only part of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a seasonal home is not a בית, why does the נביא call it a 'house'? The פסוק seems to show that a part-time dwelling is still called a house.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He objected to him' from a source

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him,
but isn't it written:
"I will strike the winter house with the summer house"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the rule רבא gave in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a home not used all year is not a בית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses the word 'house' for a seasonal dwelling. So a part-time home seems to count as a house.

steps.title: It is called a winter house, not simply a house
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a seasonal dwelling is called a house only with a qualifier, such as 'winter house'. It is never called simply 'house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: It is called a 'winter house' or a 'summer house'. It is not called a plain 'house'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his rule. He points to the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק needs to add a description, 'winter' or 'summer', to call these places a house. The מצוה of מזוזה uses the plain word 'house', and the plain word means a full, year-round home.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is called "winter house" and "summer house",
it is not called a plain "house."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּית חוֹרֶף וּבֵית קַיִץ אִיקְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers אביי's challenge from the פסוק in step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the wording: a qualified name is not the same as the plain term
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק calls it a 'house', a seasonal dwelling should count as a בית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a dwelling called simply 'house', meaning a year-round home, counts as a בית for מזוזה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires a מזוזה even on a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא again. A משנה records a dispute about a festival סוכה, and a ברייתא on it says רבי יהודה requires עירוב, מזוזה and מעשר for a סוכה, even though it is used for only seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: About a festival סוכה during the festival, רבי יהודה obligates and the חכמים exempt. And it was taught about this: רבי יהודה obligates it in עירוב, in מזוזה and in מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second, stronger challenge, this time from רבי יהודה's own words. The next step completes this challenge by blocking a possible answer, and רבא's reply comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה is lived in for only seven days, which is far from a year-round home. Yet רבי יהודה treats it as a real house and requires a מזוזה on it. This seems to contradict the year-round rule רבא gave in רבי יהודה's name.

keyTerms.meaning: The סוכה built for the festival of סוכות
'Exempt,' hold that there is no obligation
'And it was taught about it,' a ברייתא that comments on the source
The joining of courtyards that allows carrying on שבת
Tithes. Bringing produce into a house makes it obligated in tithing.

steps.confusionAlert: This is רבי יהודה himself requiring a מזוזה on a temporary dwelling. That is why it is such a sharp challenge to רבא's explanation of his view.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
A festival sukkah during the festival,
Rabbi Yehuda obligates
and the Rabbis exempt.
And it was taught concerning it:
Rabbi Yehuda obligates it in eiruv
and in mezuzah and in tithes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second objection to רבא's rule. It comes from a משנה and the ברייתא taught on it, instead of a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי יהודה requires a year-round home before it counts as a בית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה requires a מזוזה on a סוכה, which is used for only seven days. So he must count a temporary dwelling as a בית.

steps.title: Blocking the answer that the ברייתא is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי sees a possible answer coming: maybe רבי יהודה obligates the סוכה only מדרבנן. He says that could work for עירוב and מזוזה, but not for מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that these obligations are only rabbinic, that is fine for עירוב and מזוזה, which could be rabbinic. But מעשר — can you really say it is only rabbinic?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is still challenging רבא. He predicts רבא's answer ('these are only rabbinic rules') and shows that this answer does not cover all three items in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא could try to save his view by saying a סוכה counts as a בית only by rabbinic law, while by Torah law it is still not a house. אביי accepts that עירוב and מזוזה could be rabbinic here. But he argues that the rule of מעשר is hard to explain as only rabbinic. So the ברייתא still seems to show that, for רבי יהודה, a סוכה is a real בית.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say' — the גמרא predicts an answer in order to reject it
By rabbinic law (not a Torah obligation)
'Granted' — this part works, but the next part is a problem
Tithes. The ברייתא says the סוכה makes produce obligated in tithes, the way a house does
'Can one really say?' — a challenging question that expects the answer no

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new קשיא from scratch. It is the second half of אביי's challenge from step 36. He is shutting a door before רבא can walk through it.

phrases.english: And if you say: it is by rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: Meaning: רבי יהודה obligates the סוכה only rabbinically, so by Torah law רבא's view still holds.

phrases.english: granted, regarding עירוב and מזוזה,
it is possible to say they are rabbinic,
but regarding tithes,
phrases.notes: Here is the weak spot in the 'rabbinic' answer.

phrases.english: can it really be said that it is rabbinic?
phrases.notes: The question expects the answer 'no', so the challenge to רבא stands for now.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: דחיה (rejecting an answer before it is given)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge from step 36 by blocking the expected answer that the ברייתא's obligations are only rabbinic.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim (step 33) that for רבי יהודה a dwelling not built for both summer and winter is not a בית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats a סוכה as a בית for עירוב, מזוזה and מעשר. Calling all of these rabbinic fails, because מעשר is hard to explain as only a rabbinic rule. So the ברייתא seems to show that רבי יהודה treats a סוכה as a real בית.
